hours: Lunch: Fri – Sat, Dinner: Wed – Sat
bio: There are very few restaurants in Northern Ireland with a Michelin star – Ox being one of them. It all began when Belfast native Stephen Toman was working at The World's 50 Best Restaurants regular, Arpège in Paris, where he met Brittany-born maître d' Alain Kerloc'h. The two became friends and in 2013, they combined skills to open Ox in Belfast, overlooking the River Lagan. A huge window bathes diners in light, while the simplified fit-out, including chairs from a local church, belies the brio of the tasting menus. Meticulous standards and an ingredient-led philosophy are the drivers here. Each dish leaving the kitchen showcases what's in the ever-changing Ox larder, a list of which is regularly updated on the website. Throw in wines from unusual regions and a broad selection of Irish craft gins and you'll understand why booking is essential. Expect the polish of a world-class fine diner with the warmth of a neighbourhood bistro.

name: Fumée
address: Room 303-1, 3rd Floor, Hanking Financial Center, No. 9968 Shennan Avenue, Shenzhen,
bio: Fumée makes a compelling case for borderless Chinese cooking. The 16-course menu draws inspiration from the country's many provinces to create dishes that are both inventive and showcase the breadth its cuisine. A standout example is the tofu trio, inspired by the flavours of Chaoshan: three layers of tofu coated in Puning-style batter, including a scallop mousse crafted to mimic tofu's texture and a final layer of fermented tofu, all encased in a crisp shell and finished with a dollop of caviar. Ingredients are developed with equal care behind the scenes – the Shaoxing wine lees used to finish the sturgeon tendon dish, for instance, are refined using an ice-drip technique. Regular chef collaborations – including appearances by maestro Umberto Bombana of 8½ Otto e Mezzo Bombana – bring fresh perspectives to the menu. Meanwhile, a French-leaning wine list reflects founder David Pan's passion for the region.

Delicately painted ceramics, clay bowls and wooden trays provide the canvas for meticulously arranged dishes, such as seven-day aged squab grilled on the crown and served with duck liver velouté, wilted spinach and daikon foam.
